title: Top K Frequent Words
statement: Return the k most frequent words, most frequent first. Words appearing the same number of times are ordered lexicographically, smallest first.
constraints: the tie-break is lexicographic ASCENDING, while the frequency ordering is DESCENDING
hints: Count first with a dictionary. The whole problem is then how you order the distinct words.
The comparison has two keys pulling in opposite directions: higher count wins, but on a tie the SMALLER word wins. Getting one of them backwards is the bug this problem is really testing.

Sorting all distinct words is O(d log d) and perfectly acceptable. For O(d log k), keep a heap of size k whose comparator is deliberately INVERTED - the worst entry sits on top so it can be evicted - then reverse what you drain out.
complexity: O(d log k) time with a bounded heap

cases.name: tie broken lexicographically, not by first appearance
k smaller than the distinct count
